mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) consistently predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns because it reflects an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates and supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPIAUCSL growth rate exceeding 2.5% signals an inflationary environment that triggers Fed tightening, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0% and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 1.0%, it indicates a recessionary environment with accommodative policy, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE > 5.0% and FEDFUNDS < 1.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 90), the S&P 500 exhibits negative 60-day forward returns as the economy enters a recession.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO < 90 periods (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) consistently predicts positive 5-day S&P 500 returns as it reflects strong economic growth and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above 600 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month growth rate in retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% signals strong consumer demand, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS MoM growth exceeds 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 2.5% YoY and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains stable (change < 0.1%), it signals the Fed is behind the curve, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 2.5% AND FEDFUNDS change < 0.1%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS change < 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong labor market growth (PAYEMS MoM growth > 0.5%), the S&P 500 exhibits negative 20-day forward returns due to expectations of Fed tightening to combat inflation.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS MoM growth exceeds 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
